newsitem.title: UK: House of Fraser to cut jobs, sell stores.
newsitem.headline: House of Fraser to cut jobs, sell stores.

text.p: British department store group House of Fraser Plc said on Monday it is to cut around 1,000 jobs and sell three stores in a major restructuring.

The loss-making retailer said it will take a charge of between 12 and 15 million pounds ($24.51 million) to cover the restructuring, plus a separate charge of between 22 million and 25 million pounds for stock clearance.
House of Fraser to cut jobs, sell stores
The stores up for sale are Army & Navy in Eastbourne in southern England, House of Fraser in Sheffield in northern England and Binns in Scunthorpe in the north east.

The firm said no other store disposals or closures were currently planned, but the performance of all the its stores would be kept under review. The restructuing is expected to give annualised savings of about 10 million pounds ($16.34 million). Job cuts are likely to be largely in management and administration, the firm said.
Chief executive John Coleman said: "The actions announced today, as promised in October, will significantly improve the operating efficiency and the trading performance of the group."

House of Fraser also gave an update on current trading, in which it said like-for-like sales were 6.1 percent higher in the 26 weeks to January 25. This included a strong performance immediately before Christmas and during the January sales. ($1=.6119 Pound)
